## Objective
- Build a complete, playable roguelike FPS hero shooter with four classes inspired by classic fantasy magic, quick 5–10 minute matches, and rewards that carry into future runs.

## Requirements
- Don’t ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For screenshot checks, save small JPEGs at viewport width ≤1280px and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained browser game with Canvas raycasting and original fantasy classes rather than relying on game libraries or external assets.
- Matches have six waves, inter-wave upgrade choices, and persistent legacy shards.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added class selection, FPS movement/aiming, enemies, spells and class abilities, wave progression, upgrades, persistent rewards, pause/end screens, HUD, minimap, and touch controls.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Reviewing gameplay and refining implementation; movement, collisions, rendering, and controls need browser testing.

### Blocked
- Browser check is blocked because Chromium is not installed: `Browser "chromium" is not installed; expected executable at /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome.`

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` for correctness, especially enemy movement and wave completion logic.
2. Install Chromium if available, start/test the game at `http://localhost:3002`, and fix any gameplay or visual issues.
3. Save and inspect a latest small JPEG screenshot; report the tested state.
4. Summarize reasonable assumptions and completed work to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens, HUD, class cards, and controls.
- `style.css`: Game visuals and responsive/touch layouts.
- `game.js`: Game logic, raycasting renderer, controls, waves, upgrades, persistence.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` failed because Chromium is missing.
- Last change added `moveEnemy()` in `game.js`; it has not yet been wired into enemy movement.
